comment: The prologue (canon section 7): the Stopped Clock. The existing loft quest, now an arc that starts time. Plus the first winding, every newcomer's own first session (per player, not an arc).

prologue.title: The Stopped Clock
prologue.summary: The great clock stopped the night of the first hard frost. Find the escapement gear, bring it to Tace, and open the clock case: time begins again.

read-ledger.hint: the dreamer reads the repair ledger

found-gear.hint: the dreamer finds the escapement gear by the well

gave-gear.hint: the dreamer brings the gear home to Tace

unlocked.hint: the dreamer unlocks the clock case

mended-together.summary: mended by more than one dreamer
mended-together.text: Somewhere above, the great clock's hands begin to move, and the whole tower seems to breathe out. Everyone who helped feels it in their chest at once, like a held note finally sung.
mended-together.ledger: The great clock was mended by {helpers} together, and time began again in the village.

do.name: case key
do.seed: a small brass case-key on a loop of worn ribbon, warm as if just out of a pocket

do.text: Tace turns the little gear over in the lamplight, and something long held eases out of their shoulders. 'You found it. You carried it all the way home.' A breath on its teeth, a rub with their sleeve, and they fold it back into your hand with a small brass key, warm from their pocket. 'By custom the one who carries it home sets it in. The case is yours to open, friend.'
do.others: Tace turns the little gear over in the lamplight, cleans it on their sleeve, and folds it back into {actor}'s hand with a small brass key: the case is theirs to open now.

do.text: {actor} carried the escapement gear home to Tace.
Tace folds your fingers gently back around the gear. 'Yours to set, friend. The case downstairs is waiting.'
You ease the little door, then stop: the place where the escapement gear belongs stands empty, and the clock will not go without it.
Tace considers what you're holding out, and smiles a small, tired smile. 'That's kind of you. But it isn't the little thing the clock is missing.'
Tace folds your fingers gently back around the small clock. 'That one's yours, friend. By custom, it stays with you.'

You turn the little key. The small clock hesitates, then begins to tick, soft and sure, a half-beat apart from every other clock on the shelf. Tace watches with their hands folded. 'There,' they say. 'Now there's an hour here that's yours. Bell will be glad to hear it, next time you're in the square. And Mott keeps something for every new keeper, in the workshop.'

threads.text: The great clock in the tower has stopped. Its repair ledger lies open on the lectern beside it.
The repair ledger says the escapement gear rolled out of the tower and away across the square. Someone in the Lantern Square might have seen where it went.
Bell saw something bright go bouncing south, into the old well-court. It must be there somewhere: look closely.
The escapement gear lies in the moss at the old well's foot, where the ferns hid it.
You carry the escapement gear. Tace, up in the loft, has been waiting for it.
Tace has given up the case key, and the gear went back with it: by custom, the one who carries it home sets it in. The clock case in the tower waits.
Up in the Clockmaker's Loft, Tace keeps a small clock for every new keeper. Ask about the first winding.
Tace gave you a small clock of your own. Wind it, by the old custom, when you're ready.
Bell will want to meet you, down in the Lantern Square.
Bell will want to hear your clock, down in the Lantern Square.
Mott keeps something for every new keeper, in the Old Workshop north of the square.
